title: jnprofile-typescript
text: jnprofile-typescript is the TypeScript profile of jnterfaces. A profile sets up a project in one language. It has tools, for example lint, and each tool brings its packages, its parts of the config files and its recipes. A recipe is a command of the project’s Justfile, such as just lint. The profile is for a TypeScript project with npm. The installer finds such a project by its package.json or tsconfig.json.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: Run this command in a project that has the jnterfaces installer: just install --profile typescript The command installs the tools lint and typecheck. It also turns on the default roles of the profile, tasker and prose, unless you choose otherwise. The roles in the jnterfaces guide tells what each role installs. In a folder with no package.json, it first runs npm init --yes. Then add or remove a tool: just install test just uninstall lint The machine needs just and uv. uv runs node and npm from the nodejs-wheel package, so you do not install node. To install every dependency into node_modules, run just setup.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: Tool Packages Recipes lint biome just fmt, just lint typecheck typescript, @types/node just typecheck test typescript, @types/node just build, just test The tools gives each recipe and each part that a tool adds to a config file.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: A part is the piece of a shared config file that a tool owns. just install adds the part, and just uninstall takes out only that part. Your own settings stay. biome.json and tsconfig.json get an include. The installer writes the settings of the profile to a file under .agents/config/typescript/, and adds that file to extends in your file. A setting in your file wins over the setting of the profile. When the project has a biome.jsonc and no biome.json, the include goes to biome.jsonc. .gitignore and .worktreedisposable get a block of lines. A block starts and ends with a comment that names its owner. Do not edit a file under .agents/config/. Only the installer writes it. Shared files and the record in the jnterfaces guide tells you how the installer keeps a record of each part.

title: jnprofile-typescript
text: jnterfaces: the installer, and the just, jagt-protocol and cx skills. jnprofile-python: the Python profile. agent_gest_git_skills: the tasker role and its g skills.

title: The tools
text: Each tool of the profile brings its packages, its recipes and its parts. The installer adds the packages to the devDependencies of package.json with npm.

title: The tools
text: Each project of the profile gets the base, with no tool. Recipe What it does just setup Installs every dependency into node_modules, as package-lock.json says The recipes run node and npm with uvx --from 'nodejs-wheel==24.*'. The cache of npm is in .local/npm-cache. The base adds node_modules/, dist/, .local/ and *.tsbuildinfo to .gitignore. It adds node_modules/ and *.tsbuildinfo to .worktreedisposable, the list of files that a command makes again, so that they do not keep a worktree.

title: The tools
text: The package is @biomejs/biome@2. Recipe What it does just fmt Formats the code. Extra arguments go to biome: just fmt src just lint Checks the code against the rules of biome. Extra arguments go to biome: just lint --write The part is an include in biome.json. Its extends names ./.agents/config/typescript/lint.json. That file turns on the git integration of biome, so biome skips the files that git ignores. It leaves out dist, node_modules, .agents, .claude and .codex, and sets an indent of spaces and lines of at most 120 characters.

title: The tools
text: The packages are typescript@7 and @types/node@24. Recipe What it does just typecheck Checks the types with tsc and tsconfig.json. A project whose tsconfig.json finds no code yet passes The part is an include in tsconfig.json. Its extends names ./.agents/config/typescript/tsconfig.json. That file compiles src/ into dist/ for ES2023 and NodeNext modules, in strict mode, with source maps and the types of node. Its paths start with ${configDir}, so they are paths in your project, not in .agents/config/.

title: The tools
text: The packages are typescript@7 and @types/node@24, as for typecheck. The tool has the same part in tsconfig.json. When both tools are on, the include stays until both are off. Recipe What it does just build Compiles the code into dist/, with tsconfig.json just test Compiles, then runs the tests in dist/ with node --test. A project whose tsconfig.json finds no code yet passes
